mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending power increases.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE dropped by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% in a month suggests strong consumer demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies struggle with reduced output and profitability.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it indicates strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the months with PAYEMS increase > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% each in a month suggests a robust demand environment, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS increase > 5% each in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increased by more than 5% each in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure during a tightening cycle, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings grow.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the quarters where GDPC1 increased by more than 1%.
